## Description
The Terminal Capsule's command history has three independent React state owners even though the UI presents it as one live history. On current `main`, sending a command writes the sender hook's state and `localStorage`, but the mounted History popover and ghost-completion field retain their own initial snapshots. The user can send a command, open History immediately, and see an empty/stale list; typing its prefix does not offer the just-sent command until remount.

This contradicts the continuous Session input experience in [VISION.md](https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/blob/main/VISION.md) and the TerminalCapsule's command/history interaction. It is a **post-closure residual defect** relative to [#1034](https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/issues/1034) and [#2710](https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/issues/2710): those accepted the composer and saved-command actions, but their acceptance does not establish cross-component reactive history synchronization after a new send.

## Reproduction
1. Open a Web Terminal Capsule with a fresh `nession_command_history` localStorage key. Keep the Capsule mounted.
2. Type `echo nession-history-probe` and Send; `useCapsuleState.send()` records it.
3. Open the History popover without unmounting/remounting the Capsule: it still shows `No matching commands`.
4. Type `echo nes`: ghost completion is absent despite the command now existing in localStorage.
5. Remount the Capsule: both readers initialize from storage and the entry appears. This last step distinguishes snapshot invalidation from failed persistence.

**Verification status:** Static call-chain proof on current main; Chromium execution has not yet been performed.

## Root Cause
- [`useCommandHistory.ts`](https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/blob/main/web/src/product/terminal/hooks/useCommandHistory.ts): each hook invocation initializes its **own** `useState(loadFromStorage)`; `addEntry` only updates that invocation and writes localStorage, without any subscription/broadcast or shared owner.
- [`useCapsuleState.ts`](https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/blob/main/web/src/product/terminal/capsule/state/useCapsuleState.ts) calls `useCommandHistory()` for `addEntry` and owns the send action.
- [`CapsuleHistoryPopover.tsx`](https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/blob/main/web/src/product/terminal/capsule/CapsuleHistoryPopover.tsx) calls the hook again for `filterHistory`.
- [`CapsuleGhostInput.tsx`](https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/blob/main/web/src/product/terminal/capsule/CapsuleGhostInput.tsx) calls it a third time for ghost candidates.
- [`useCommandHistory.test.ts`](https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/blob/main/web/src/product/terminal/hooks/__tests__/integration/useCommandHistory.test.ts) tests only one hook instance at a time; it does not assert multiple mounted consumers see a mutation.

The browser `storage` event does not notify other hook instances within the same document, and this hook does not subscribe to it anyway.

## Impact
New commands and recency changes are invisible to the active History and ghost suggestions until a remount. Separate mounted Capsule instances can also overwrite one another's persisted history from stale snapshots. This makes the UI inconsistent with the action the user just completed.

## Fix Direction
Give command-history state one reactive owner shared by all Capsule consumers; keep the existing bounded 500-entry persistence, deduplication and command-send semantics. Prefer an owner-local external store/context or equivalent shared subscription rather than independent `useState` snapshots. Preserve cross-tab behavior where supported; do not introduce server-side history, protocol changes, a global Workspace store, or a new command interaction.

## Location
`web/src/product/terminal/hooks/useCommandHistory.ts`, `web/src/product/terminal/capsule/state/useCapsuleState.ts`, `web/src/product/terminal/capsule/CapsuleHistoryPopover.tsx`, `web/src/product/terminal/capsule/CapsuleGhostInput.tsx`.

### Success Criteria
- [ ] SC-01: With the Capsule kept mounted, sending or running a new command makes it immediately available in the History popover and prefix ghost completion, without reload/remount; repeat sends update recency and never create duplicate entries.
- [ ] SC-02: Two simultaneously mounted history consumers observe add/remove/clear consistently, and persistence remains bounded to 500 entries; a stale consumer cannot restore deleted entries.

**Scenario selection:** SC-01 → SCN-02 (Chromium/Playwright Web interaction; open popover and assert rendered rows and ghost suffix). SC-02 → SCN-01 (deterministic multi-subscriber integration test with storage assertions). Both have feasible PR-head CI execution paths; no staging credentials are needed.
